meta.title: Nurse Jill's Test Week Tips
meta.textType: functional: a talk with examples, and a set of steps

paragraphs: On Thursday, March fourth, Nurse Jill came to the school library for the club hour. She stood next to an easel with a big poster. The title of the poster was "Test Week Plan." Teacher Kim sat at the back, and the Explorers sat at a table with their notebooks. "The tests start on Monday," said Nurse Jill. "My advice is simple: look after your health, and you will feel fit."

"The poster has five tips, and I will give you an example for each." "Tip one is sleep." "Say good night by nine o'clock, and use a soft pillow." "Tip two is eat." "A healthy breakfast, such as rice, an egg, and fruit, gives you energy." "Tip three is drink." "For example, put a glass of water on your desk." "Tip four is move." "A ten-minute walk is good exercise, and it helps you relax." "Tip five is ask." "Tell an adult if you feel unwell." Lily wrote each tip in her notebook with one example under it.

Next, Nurse Jill gave each child a small card called "A Calm Test Morning." Lily held hers beside her notebook. "Here are five steps for the morning of a test," said Nurse Jill. "First, drink water." "Next, eat breakfast." "Then check your bag: pencil, ruler, extra pencil." "After that, walk to school slowly." "Finally, take three slow breaths." "Get up early, so that there is time for every step." "Prepare your school clothes the evening before, too."

"What if I cannot sleep?" asked Leo. "You may read a quiet book, but please do not use a screen," said Nurse Jill. "Stay in bed and close your eyes." "Your body can rest, even if you are not asleep." "How much water is enough?" asked May. "One glass in the morning and one glass at school is a good start," said Nurse Jill.

Then she spoke more slowly. "A headache, a stomachache, or a cough in test week is a good reason to tell an adult," she said. "These signs may mean a cold, or they might mean only a hard week." "A teacher or a parent can help, and you can come to my room." "Please do not stay silent."

At the end, Mia said, "I will say good night at nine o'clock." "I will put my screen away at eight," said Leo. "That is a good plan," said Nurse Jill with a smile. Lily put the card in her notebook, and the club hour ended.
